headline: Melanin reduction, side by side
footnote: In-vitro lab test on a skin-identical model vs an international brand's Alpha Arbutin 2% serum.
caption: Minimalist ran an in-vitro (lab) test on a skin-identical model, comparing this serum with an Alpha Arbutin 2% serum from an international brand that offers active-based products. The benchmark reduced melanin by 56%; Minimalist Alpha Arbutin 2% reduced melanin concentration by 70%.
layout_description: White canvas. Wordmark + 'Hide Nothing.' top-left, headline across the top; the real pack large on the left; on the right a two-row table, ours vs the benchmark: 'Alpha Arbutin strength' 2% vs 2% (like for like), 'Melanin reduction (lab test)' 70% vs 56%. Footnote states the test; quiet 'Shop now' label bottom-left.
adaptation_notes: Kept from the reference (Deconstruct, 129 days): the side-by-side 'v/s' header and one pack as the hero. Replaced its European-vs-Korean contrast with the page's own published comparison: an in-vitro test vs a benchmark Alpha Arbutin 2% serum (F12, F13). The strength row shows the comparison is like for like (ASCI Chapter IV). The page's derived '25% more reduction' is not used: the two raw results are shown with the method. Dropped 'India's 1st' (superlative) and the claims list. CLM-12 (comparison) is expected for this format; the basis is in the footnote. Risk High: a reviewer confirms the test report is on file.

verdict.label: Do not publish
verdict.detail: At least one finding would put the ad at legal or brand risk. Export is disabled until it is fixed.

findings.message: The ad's lead benefit is cutting melanin, the skin's own pigment, and nowhere does it tie that to dark spots or uneven patches; with the test run on a dark-skin ('Black skin') tissue model, '70% melanin reduction' reads as making skin lighter. It is also a melanin structure/function claim (CLM-24), so the same wording in the primary text and the on-image row needs the same change.
findings.fix: Lead with the concern, not the pigment, e.g. 'For dark spots: two serums, tested side by side in a lab', and relabel the matching 'melanin' lines in the body and table as a lab skin-model result rather than a change in the viewer's skin. Have legal confirm the final wording.

layout_description: White canvas. findings.message: ISO 24444:2019 is the in-vivo method for SPF only; a PA rating comes from a separate UVA test (such as ISO 24442 or ISO 24443), so this line credits PA++++ to a test that doesn't measure it. findings.fix: Separate the two results, e.g. 'In-vivo SPF test (ISO 24444:2019): SPF 50 confirmed. PA++++ per [the UVA test named in the report].' If the report has no UVA test, attach substantiation for PA++++ before this runs.
